items.title: What It Takes to Be Free
items.description: We spend our lives trying to find our power and our freedom. items.title: What Is Your Refugium?
items.description: For courage, says Bulgarian folk wisdom instructs, keep a horse chestnut in your pocket. Even as a child, I was mistrustful of superstition. But every autumn, I would pick up dozens of them from the sidewalks of Sofia and fill my pockets — not as a spell against fear but as an ode to joy. Conkers, as the English call them, spun me up in delight — shiny as mahogany, smooth as river stones, tiny planets from some other universe, the wonder-smitten eyes of some prehistoric creature. items.title: The Wildest Bet Is the Winning Bet
items.description: We place life’s bets by countless calculations of probability, conscious and unconscious, only to discover over and over how short they fall of the wildest reaches of the possible, which always includes but exceeds the probable. It helps to remember that we ourselves are children of improbability, that everything we treasure exists not because it had to, not because it was likely or necessary, but because the universe took a gamble against the staggering odds otherwise. items.title: How to Be Transformed When Things Fall Apart
items.description: "Only to the extent that we expose ourselves over and over to annihilation can that which is indestructible be found in us."

items.title: When Your Parents Are Dying: Some of the Simplest, Most Difficult and Redemptive Life-Advice You’ll Ever Receive
items.description: "Death makes human beings seem like very small containers that are packed so densely we can only be aware of a fraction of what's inside us from moment to moment."

items.title: The Most Important Thing to Remember About Your Mother
items.description: "It is not easy to give closeness and freedom, safety plus danger."

items.title: Walt Whitman’s Advice on Living a Vibrant and Rewarding Life
items.description: “Love the earth and sun and the animals… re-examine all you have been told at school or church or in any book, dismiss whatever insults your own soul…”

items.title: Bob Dylan on the Unconscious Mind and the Ideal Conditions for Creative Work
items.description: "People have a hard time accepting anything that overwhelms them."

items.title: Dostoyevsky, Just After His Death Sentence Was Repealed, on the Meaning of Life
items.description: "To be a human being among people and to remain one forever, no matter in what circumstances, not to grow despondent and not to lose heart — that’s what life is all about, that's its task."

items.title: Sylvia Plath on Living with the Darkness and Making Art from the Barely Bearable Lightness of Being
items.description: "One has to shut off that nagging part of the mind and go on without it with bravo and philosophy."

items.title: Marcus Aurelius on the Good Luck of Your Bad Luck
items.description: "What happened could have happened to anyone, but not everyone could have carried on."

items.title: The Baloney Detection Kit: Carl Sagan’s Timeless Tenets of Critical Thinking
items.description: Necessary cognitive fortification against propaganda, pseudoscience, and general falsehood.
